newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - June 9.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest - June 9.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING
WALLDORF - Hamburg-based advertising agency Kolle Rebbe wins the account of bottled water brand Apollinaris, beating out Scholz & Friends and Young & Rubicam. (Kress)
FRANKFURT - Stefan A. Wagemanns becomes trade marketing director of Swiss chocolate manufacturer Lindt & Spruengli, effective July 2. (Horizont)
WALLDORF - Advertising agency JK wins the seven-figure account of prefabricated house manufacturer Okal, beating out KNSK, BBDO, Rahmel & Partner and previous account holder ICW Wilkens.(Kress)
WALLDORF - News channel CNN will launch its first German-language service on June 9 in Germany's most populous state, North Rhine-Westphalia. (Reuter)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:
BONN - Deutsche Telekom AG plans to charge pay-TV stations 90 million marks ($52 million) for inclusion in its cable network, 30 times to current price, reports news magazine Der Spiegel.(Reuter)

WALLDORF - Internet surfers will soon have to pay fees similar to those television viewers currently have to pay. Der Spiegel reports this is because television programming is now available on the Internet at almost the same time it is shown on TV.
(Kress)

MUNICH - Media giant Bertelsmann has formed a strategic alliance with information service Reed Elsevier Deutschland to provide online data on the transportation industry. The companies plan to integrate their marketing of internet services, the Bertlesmann industry information division says.
(Reuter)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:
BONN - The director of development at car maker Opel, Juergen Stockmar, plans to leave the company this week, Der Spiegel reports. (Reuter)

FRANKFURT - Rail systems company Adtranz says a joint venture in which it participates has won a contract in Australia worth 130 million European currency units (ECU) to make electric railcars. Adtranz says the deal was the largest passenger rail vehicle contract in Australia for nearly 10 years. The cars are to be designed by Adtranz but made in Australia by joint venture partner Evans Deakin Industries Ltd. (Reuter)

NUREMBERG - Market research company GfK plans expansion with more growth abroad and the conversion of minority holdings to majority holdings. The company plans to increase its turnover to 650 million marks by the year 2000. (Sueddeutsche Zeitung)
PEOPLE NEWS:

WALLDORF - Francis Edwards has taken over the operations of home-shopping channel QVC in Germany. Rainer Vogel, who held the job previously, will remain on the board of the Duesseldorf-based station. (Kress)
